topic: Peptides your body makes: motilin, the gut's own fasting timer and hunger signal. Motilin is a 22-amino-acid peptide made by endocrine cells in the mucosa of the upper small intestine, identified in the 1970s from pig upper intestine (Kitazawa & Kaiya, Front Endocrinol 2021); discovery dated 1972 (Deloose et al., Nat Rev Endocrinol 2019). In fasting humans plasma motilin rises in cycles about every 100 minutes (Kitazawa & Kaiya 2021). The migrating motor complex (MMC) is a cyclic motility pattern of the stomach and small bowel during fasting, interrupted by feeding; phase III is the most active burst of contractions, starting in the antrum or duodenum and migrating distally; motilin can induce antral-origin phase III (Deloose et al., Nat Rev Gastroenterol Hepatol 2012). Tack et al., Gut 2016: hunger ratings during gastric phase III (62.5) were higher than in phase I (27.4); motilin induced premature gastric phase III and a rise in hunger; 'motilin-induced gastric phase III is a hunger signal from GIT in man'. Motilin and its receptor exist only as pseudogenes in rodents (Deloose et al. 2019).

PEPTIDES YOUR BODY MAKES

Your empty gut squeezes on a 100-minute timer.

Meet motilin

Motilin

A 22-amino-acid peptide hormone.

Made in your upper small intestine. Found in 1972.

Between meals

~100

minutes

Motilin in your blood rises in waves.

1

2
A strong squeeze starts in the stomach.
3
It sweeps down the gut. Eating stops it.

It feels like hunger.
